_comment: What this skill says out loud, declared so it can be recorded ahead of time.
Lesson intros are NOT listed here — generate-voice.mjs collects every
lessons.json `params.play.audioPrompt` itself, so authoring a lesson never
What belongs here is speech that lives in the skill's code, and the rule is
the same one that governs feature flags: declare only what something
actually says. Every line below is spoken by CountTray, and a phrase nothing
says is a clip nobody hears and an API call somebody paid for.
This is the Phase 1 script — levels 1 to 7. Each later phase adds the lines
its own engine speaks. Nothing is recorded yet: until `npm run voice:record`
is run, every line takes the live TTS path, which is slower and never silent.
_numberComment: CountTray counts aloud in words — `say(n)` returns 'seven', not '7' — so the
words are what get recorded. Levels 1-7 reach 12 at most; the list runs to
twenty because Phase 2's ten-frames and Phase 3's number path will use all of
it, and a word costs one clip whether or not it is a round number.
There is deliberately no `numberRange` here. That records the *digits* '0'
to '20', and nothing in this skill speaks a digit yet — JumpLine will, in
Phase 3, when it names positions past twenty. Adding it now would buy 21
_promptsComment: The question itself, as the Read-aloud button says it.
Only the fixed ones. A lesson's `prompts.default` is not collected — the
activity interpolates it, so 'What is {a} plus {b}?' could never match a
recording — and for adding zero and adding one that is right: those two vary
over more than a hundred pairs and belong on live TTS.
prompts: Count them all. How many altogether?
Put the groups together, then count them all.
Start with the bigger number, then count on.
_templateComment: A template is expanded into one recorded line per value, which is how a
prompt containing a number gets recorded at all.
Worth it only where the range is small and matches the lesson: Count On
draws its first addend from 4 to 9, so this is six fixed sentences rather
than one dynamic one. Keep these values tracking lessons.json — count-on's
_phrasesComment: Everything else CountTray says in passing. One line, so far.
_groupsComment: Several ways of saying the same thing, so praise does not become wallpaper.
`playAnswerSound` picks one on every answer, which is why these are recorded
rather than spoken live: a network round trip between a child and their next
question is worse than saying nothing.

phrases: Good try. Let's count them together.
